en: Verbs pozvať, piť, niesť, jesť, stať sa
t: pozvať, piť, niesť, jesť, stať sa feʼllari

u6-l1.0.note.en: Ask for it politely: Jedálny lístok, prosím.
u6-l1.0.note.t: Uni xushmuomalalik bilan soʻrang: Jedálny lístok, prosím.

u6-l1.1.note.en: A Slovak lunch nearly always starts with a hot soup.
u6-l1.1.note.t: Slovakiyada tushlik deyarli doim issiq shoʻrva bilan boshlanadi.

u6-l1.4.note.en: Menus name meat after the animal: kuracie mäso = chicken, bravčové mäso = pork.
u6-l1.4.note.t: Menyuda goʻsht hayvon nomi bilan ataladi: kuracie mäso = tovuq goʻshti, bravčové mäso = choʻchqa goʻshti.

u6-l1.5.note.en: **veľmi** = very: Ryba je veľmi dobrá. = The fish is very good.
u6-l1.5.note.t: **veľmi** = juda: Ryba je veľmi dobrá. = Baliq juda mazali (ovqat haqida dobrý = mazali).

u6-l1.7.note.en: A typical side dish (príloha) with chicken or fish.
u6-l1.7.note.t: Tovuq yoki baliq bilan beriladigan odatiy garnir (príloha).

u6-l1.8.note.en: Always plural, like English “chips”: Hranolky **sú** dobré.

u6-l1.9.question.en: Which one is a side dish?

u6-l1.10.why.en: The menu is **jedálny lístok**. Jedálny has the masculine ending (short, like čierny), so it needs a masculine noun; jedlo and mäso are neuter.
u6-l1.10.why.t: Menyu — **jedálny lístok**. Jedálny erkak jinsi qoʻshimchasi bilan tugaydi (čierny kabi qisqa), shuning uchun erkak jinsidagi ot kerak; jedlo va mäso esa oʻrta jinsda.

en: An adjective takes the gender of its noun, after je too. Ryba is feminine, so it's **dobrá**. Dobrý is the masculine form.
Ryba is one thing, so byť takes **je** (is). Sú is for two or more, they are.
t: Sifat je soʻzidan keyin ham oʻz otining jinsiga moslashadi. Ryba ayol jinsida, shuning uchun **dobrá**. Dobrý — erkak jinsi shakli.
Ryba — bitta narsa, shuning uchun byť **je** boʻladi. Sú ikki va undan ortiq narsa uchun.

u6-l1.13.why.en: **Hranolky** is always plural, like English “chips”, so the verb is **sú** (they are). Je is for one thing.
u6-l1.13.why.t: **Hranolky** doim koʻplikda boʻladi (oʻzbekchada birlik boʻlsa ham), shuning uchun feʼl **sú** keladi. Je bitta narsa uchun.

en: An adjective takes the gender of its noun, after je too. Polievka is feminine, so it's **dobrá**. Dobrý is the masculine form.
Soup is **polievka**; jedlo means food or a dish. Jedlo is also neuter, so it wouldn't fit dobrá.
t: Sifat je soʻzidan keyin ham oʻz otining jinsiga moslashadi. Polievka ayol jinsida, shuning uchun **dobrá**. Dobrý — erkak jinsi shakli.
«Shoʻrva» — **polievka**, jedlo esa «ovqat, taom». Jedlo oʻrta jinsda ham, shuning uchun dobrá unga mos kelmaydi.

u6-l2.0.note.en: The waiter's question (formal). You may also hear: Čo si prajete?
u6-l2.0.note.t: Ofitsiantning savoli («siz» shaklida). Bunday ham eshitishingiz mumkin: Čo si prajete?

u6-l2.1.note.en: After **dám si** use the accusative: polievka → polievk**u**, ryba → ryb**u**.
u6-l2.1.note.t: **dám si** soʻzlaridan keyin akuzatív (tushum kelishigi) keladi: polievka → polievk**u**, ryba → ryb**u**.

u6-l2.2.question.en: A waiter says this. What does he want to know?
u6-l2.2.question.t: Ofitsiant shunday deydi. U nimani bilmoqchi?

u6-l2.2.why.en: **Čo** is what, and **dať si** is to have (food or a drink): Čo si dáte? is the waiter's polite “What will you have?”
u6-l2.2.why.t: **Čo** — «nima», **dať si** esa ovqat yoki ichimlik «olmoq»: Čo si dáte? — ofitsiantning hurmatli «Nima olasiz?» savoli.

u6-l2.3.en.en: I'll have the fish and chips.
u6-l2.3.en.t: Men baliq va kartoshka fri olaman.

u6-l2.3.why.en: The fish is what you'll have, the object, so ryba changes -a to **-u**: dám si **rybu**. Ryby is the plural.
u6-l2.3.why.t: Baliq — siz oladigan narsa, toʻldiruvchi, shuning uchun ryba soʻzida -a oʻrniga **-u** keladi: dám si **rybu**. Ryby — koʻplik.

u6-l2.4.note.en: Answer the same way: Dám si minerálku. Or: Prosím si minerálku.
u6-l2.4.note.t: Xuddi shunday javob bering: Dám si minerálku. Yoki: Prosím si minerálku.

en: After **dám si**, use the accusative: feminine káva changes -a to **-u**, **kávu**.
The speaker is **ja**, so dať ends in **-m**: **dám** si. Dáte is the vy form, as in the waiter's Čo si dáte?
t: **Dám si** iborasidan keyin akuzatív (tushum kelishigi) keladi: ayol jinsidagi káva soʻzida -a oʻrniga **-u**, **kávu**.
Gapiruvchi — **ja**, shuning uchun dať **-m** bilan tugaydi: **dám** si (olaman). Dáte — vy shakli, ofitsiantning Čo si dáte? savolidagi kabi.

u6-l2.6.note.en: Answer: Chutí mi. (I like it.) or Nechutí mi. (I don't like it.) Formal: Chutí vám?
u6-l2.6.note.t: Javob: Chutí mi. (Menga yoqyapti.) yoki Nechutí mi. (Menga yoqmayapti.) «Siz» shaklida: Chutí vám?

u6-l2.7.question.en: Your soup is delicious. Lucia asks “Chutí ti?”. What do you say?
u6-l2.7.question.t: Shoʻrvangiz juda mazali. Lusiya «Chutí ti?» deb soʻraydi. Nima deysiz?

u6-l2.7.why.en: The soup is delicious, so answer yes. **Ne-** makes a verb negative: nechutí mi means “I don't like it”.
u6-l2.7.why.t: Shoʻrva mazali, demak «ha» deb javob berasiz: **Chutí mi**. **Ne-** feʼlni inkor qiladi: nechutí mi «menga yoqmayapti» degani.

u6-l2.8.note.en: It agrees like other adjectives, but with short endings: horúc**i** čaj, horúc**a** polievka, horúc**e** jedlo.
u6-l2.8.note.t: Boshqa sifatlar kabi moslashadi, lekin qisqa qoʻshimchalar bilan: horúc**i** čaj, horúc**a** polievka, horúc**e** jedlo.

u6-l2.12.why.en: Polievka is feminine, so horúci takes its short feminine ending **-a**: horúc**a**. Horúci is for masculine words (čaj), horúce for neuter (jedlo).
u6-l2.12.why.t: Polievka ayol jinsida, shuning uchun horúci qisqa ayol jinsi qoʻshimchasi **-a** ni oladi: horúc**a**. Horúci erkak jinsi (čaj), horúce oʻrta jins (jedlo) uchun.

u6-l2.13.why.en: Torta is feminine, so the adjective ends in **-á**: sladk**á**. Sladký is masculine, sladké neuter.
u6-l2.13.why.t: Torta ayol jinsida, shuning uchun sifat **-á** bilan tugaydi: sladk**á**. Sladký — erkak jinsi, sladké — oʻrta jins.

en: After **dáme si**, use the accusative: feminine ryba changes -a to **-u**, **rybu**, just like polievku.
“We” is **my**, so dať takes the my ending **-me**: **dáme** si. Dám is the ja form.
t: **Dáme si** iborasidan keyin akuzatív keladi: ayol jinsidagi ryba soʻzida -a oʻrniga **-u**, **rybu**, xuddi polievku kabi.
«Biz» — **my**, shuning uchun dať **-me** bilan tugaydi: **dáme** si, oʻzbekchadagi -miz kabi (olamiz). Dám — ja shakli.

en: **S** means “with”. The noun after it takes the instrumental case (the “with” case).
Masculine nouns add **-om**, neuter nouns change -o to **-om**. Feminine nouns change **-a** to **-ou**.
Before a word starting with s, z, š or ž, **s** becomes **so**: so syr**om**.
t: **S** = «bilan», lekin u otdan oldin turadi: s mliekom = sut bilan. Undan keyingi ot inštrumentál kelishigida boʻladi («bilan» kelishigi; oʻzbek tilida bunday kelishik yoʻq).
Erkak jinsidagi otlarga **-om** qoʻshiladi, oʻrta jinsda -o oʻrniga **-om** keladi. Ayol jinsida **-a** oʻrniga **-ou** keladi.
s, z, š yoki ž bilan boshlanadigan soʻzdan oldin **s** oʻrniga **so** ishlatiladi: so syr**om**.

u6-l3.1.question.en: How do you say “tea with lemon”?

u6-l3.1.why.en: After **s** (with), masculine nouns take the instrumental ending **-om**: citrón → citrón**om**.
u6-l3.1.why.t: **s** (bilan) soʻzidan keyin erkak jinsidagi otlar inštrumentál («bilan» kelishigi) qoʻshimchasi **-om** ni oladi: citrón → citrón**om**.

u6-l3.2.why.en: After **s** (with), neuter nouns change -o to **-om**: mlieko → mliek**om**.
u6-l3.2.why.t: **s** (bilan) soʻzidan keyin oʻrta jins otlarida -o oʻrniga **-om** keladi: mlieko → mliek**om**.

u6-l3.3.why.en: After **s**, feminine nouns change -a to **-ou**: ryž**ou**. Ryžu is the object form: it goes after dám si, like rybu, not after s.
u6-l3.3.why.t: **s** soʻzidan keyin ayol jinsidagi otlarda -a oʻrniga **-ou** keladi: ryž**ou**. Ryžu — toʻldiruvchi shakli: u s soʻzidan keyin emas, rybu kabi dám si iborasidan keyin keladi.

en: **S** becomes **so** before a word starting with s, z, š or ž, as syrom does: **so** syrom.
After **s** (with), masculine nouns take the instrumental ending **-om**: syr → **syrom**.
t: **S** soʻzi s, z, š yoki ž bilan boshlanadigan soʻz oldidan **so** boʻladi, syrom esa s bilan boshlanadi: **so** syrom.
Oʻzbekchada «bilan»ning oʻzi yetarli, slovakchada esa s soʻzidan keyin ot ham oʻzgaradi: erkak jinsida **-om**, syr → **syrom**.

u6-l3.5.why.en: **S** becomes **so** before a word starting with s, z, š or ž, as syrom does. Mliekom and ryžou take plain s.
u6-l3.5.why.t: s, z, š yoki ž bilan boshlanadigan soʻz oldidan **s** oʻrniga **so** keladi, syrom esa s bilan boshlanadi. Mliekom va ryžou oddiy s bilan keladi.

u6-l3.6.why.en: After **s**, masculine nouns add **-om**, names too: Tomáš**om**. Tomáša is the object form, as in Hľadám Tomáša.
u6-l3.6.why.t: **s** soʻzidan keyin erkak jinsidagi otlar, ismlar ham, **-om** oladi: Tomáš**om** (Tomash bilan). Tomáša — toʻldiruvchi shakli, masalan Hľadám Tomáša.

en: Adjectives change too. Masculine and neuter: **-ý** → **-ým**, **-é** → **-ým**. Feminine: **-á** → **-ou**, the same ending as the noun.
t: Sifatlar ham oʻzgaradi. Erkak va oʻrta jinsda: **-ý** → **-ým**, **-é** → **-ým**. Ayol jinsida: **-á** → **-ou**, xuddi otdagi kabi.

en: Emma is talking to a new friend.
I'll have coffee with cold milk.
t: Men sovuq sut bilan qahva olaman.

u6-l3.9.en.en: Lucia is with a good friend.

u6-l3.9.why.en: After s, a feminine adjective takes **-ou**, the same ending as kamarátk**ou**: dobr**ou**. Dobrým is for masculine and neuter nouns.
u6-l3.9.why.t: s soʻzidan keyin ayol jinsidagi sifat **-ou** oladi, xuddi kamarátk**ou** soʻzidagi kabi: dobr**ou**. Dobrým erkak va oʻrta jins uchun.

u6-l3.10.en.en: Tomáš is talking to a new friend.

u6-l3.10.why.en: Kamarát is masculine, so after s its adjective ends in **-ým**: nov**ým**. Novou is the feminine form, for kamarátkou.
u6-l3.10.why.t: Kamarát erkak jinsida, shuning uchun s soʻzidan keyin uning sifati **-ým** bilan tugaydi: nov**ým**. Novou — ayol jinsi shakli, kamarátkou uchun.

u6-l3.11.prompt.en: I'll have tea with cold milk.
u6-l3.11.prompt.t: Men sovuq sut bilan choy olaman.

en: Mlieko is neuter, so after s its adjective ends in **-ým**: **studeným**. Studenou is the feminine form.
**S** becomes **so** before a word starting with s, z, š or ž. The next word, studeným, starts with s: **so** studeným.
After **s** (with), neuter nouns change -o to **-om**: mlieko → **mliekom**.
t: Mlieko oʻrta jinsda, shuning uchun s soʻzidan keyin uning sifati **-ým** bilan tugaydi: **studeným**. Studenou — ayol jinsi shakli.
**S** soʻzi s, z, š yoki ž bilan boshlanadigan soʻz oldidan **so** boʻladi. Keyingi soʻz studeným s bilan boshlanadi: **so** studeným.
**S** (bilan) soʻzidan keyin oʻrta jins otlarida -o oʻrniga **-om** keladi: mlieko → **mliekom** (sut bilan).

u6-l3.12.why.en: After **s**, masculine names add **-om**: Marek → Marek**om**. Mareka is the object form, as in Hľadám Mareka.
u6-l3.12.why.t: **s** soʻzidan keyin erkak ismlari **-om** oladi: Marek → Marek**om**. Mareka — toʻldiruvchi shakli, masalan Hľadám Mareka.

u6-l4.0.note.en: To say you're paying: Zaplatím. (I'll pay.)
u6-l4.0.note.t: Oʻzingiz toʻlashingizni aytish uchun: Zaplatím. (Men toʻlayman.)

u6-l4.1.note.en: The waiter wants to know how you'll split the bill. Answer: Spolu. or Osobitne.
u6-l4.1.note.t: Ofitsiant hisobni qanday toʻlashingizni bilmoqchi. Javob: Spolu. yoki Osobitne.

u6-l4.2.question.en: The waiter asks “Spolu alebo osobitne?”. You're paying for everyone. What do you say?
u6-l4.2.question.t: Ofitsiant «Spolu alebo osobitne?» deb soʻraydi. Siz hamma uchun toʻlaysiz. Nima deysiz?

u6-l4.3.note.en: **Domov** = home (where you're heading). Formal: Ako idete domov?
u6-l4.3.note.t: **Domov** = uyga (borish yoʻnalishi). «Siz» shaklida: Ako idete domov?

u6-l4.4.note.en: There's no word for “by”: the vehicle takes the instrumental. autobus → autobus**om**.
u6-l4.4.note.t: Oʻzbekchadagi «avtobusda» kabi, alohida soʻz kerak emas: transport nomi inštrumentálda keladi. autobus → autobus**om**.

u6-l4.5.why.en: **Autobus** is a bus (a car is auto), and the instrumental ending **-om** does the job of English “by”.
u6-l4.5.why.t: **Autobus** — avtobus (mashina — auto). Inštrumentál qoʻshimchasi **-om** bu yerda oʻzbekcha «avtobusda» degandagi -da vazifasini bajaradi.

en: Put the vehicle in the instrumental, with no **s**: Idem vlak**om**. = I'm going by train.
The endings are the ones you know: **-om** for masculine and neuter, **-ou** for feminine.
**Cestovať** (to travel) goes like študovať: cestuj**em**, cestuj**eš**, cestuj**e**…
t: Transport nomi **s** qoʻshmasdan, inštrumentálda («bilan» kelishigida) keladi: Idem vlak**om**. = Poyezdda ketyapman.
Qoʻshimchalar sizga tanish: erkak va oʻrta jinsda **-om**, ayol jinsida **-ou**.
**Cestovať** (sayohat qilmoq) študovať kabi tuslanadi: cestuj**em**, cestuj**eš**, cestuj**e**…

u6-l4.7.en.en: Tomáš is travelling home by train.

u6-l4.7.why.en: How you travel takes the instrumental, with no s: masculine vlak adds **-om**, vlak**om**.
u6-l4.7.why.t: Nimada borishni aytganda transport nomi s qoʻshmasdan inštrumentálda keladi: erkak jinsidagi vlak **-om** oladi, vlak**om** (poyezdda).

u6-l4.8.why.en: For how you travel, the vehicle takes the instrumental without s: lietadl**om**. S lietadlom would mean “with a plane”.
u6-l4.8.why.t: Nimada borishni aytganda transport nomi **s qoʻshmasdan** inštrumentálda keladi: lietadl**om**. S lietadlom «samolyot bilan birga» degani boʻlardi.

u6-l4.9.en.en: Lucia is going home by tram.

u6-l4.9.why.en: Električka is feminine, so for how you travel it changes -a to **-ou**: električk**ou**. Električku is the object form.
u6-l4.9.why.t: Električka ayol jinsida, shuning uchun nimada borishni aytganda -a oʻrniga **-ou** keladi: električk**ou**. Električku — toʻldiruvchi shakli.

u6-l4.10.note.en: Idem pešo. = I'm walking. By bike is different too: **na bicykli**.
u6-l4.10.note.t: Idem pešo. = Piyoda ketyapman. Velosipedda ham boshqacha aytiladi: **na bicykli**.

en: How you travel takes the instrumental, with no s: masculine taxík adds **-om**, **taxíkom**.
“We” is **my**, so ísť takes the my form **ideme**. Idem is for ja.
t: Transport nomi s qoʻshmasdan inštrumentálda keladi: taxík → **taxíkom**. Bu yerda -om oʻzbekcha «taksida»dagi -da vazifasini bajaradi.
«Biz» — **my**, shuning uchun ísť my shaklida keladi: **ideme** (ketyapmiz). Idem ja uchun.

u6-l4.14.note.en: In the plural, the noun after s ends in **-mi** or **-ami**: s kamarát**mi**, s kamarátk**ami**.
u6-l4.14.note.t: Koʻplikda s soʻzidan keyin ot **-mi** yoki **-ami** oladi: s kamarát**mi**, s kamarátk**ami**.

u6-l4.16.en.en: Lucia is going home with her friends.

u6-l4.16.why.en: Her friends are more than one, and after **s** plural nouns end in **-mi** or **-ami**: kamarátky → kamarátk**ami**.
u6-l4.16.why.t: Dugonalar bir nechta, **s** soʻzidan keyin esa koʻplikdagi otlar **-mi** yoki **-ami** bilan tugaydi: kamarátky → kamarátk**ami**.

en: Pronouns have their own instrumental forms. After **s** they mean “with me, with you…”.
t: Olmoshlarning oʻz inštrumentál shakllari bor. **s** soʻzidan keyin ular «men bilan, sen bilan…» maʼnosini beradi.
mnou oldidan **s** oʻrniga **so** keladi: so mnou.

en: Mrs Horváthová is here. We're talking to her.
t: Horvatova xonim shu yerda. Biz u bilan gaplashyapmiz.

u6-l5.1.why.en: **So mnou** is with me (with us would be s nami), and ideš is the ty form: are you coming?
u6-l5.1.why.t: **So mnou** — «men bilan» («biz bilan» s nami boʻlardi), ideš esa ty shakli: «borasanmi?».

u6-l5.2.en.en: Tomáš is here. Lucia is talking to him.
u6-l5.2.en.t: Tomash shu yerda. Lusiya u bilan gaplashyapti.

u6-l5.2.why.en: Tomáš is on (he), and after s, on becomes **ním**. Ňou is for ona; ho is the object form, as in Mám ho rád.
u6-l5.2.why.t: Tomash — on (u), s soʻzidan keyin esa on **ním** boʻladi. Ňou — ona uchun, ho esa toʻldiruvchi shakli, masalan Mám ho rád.

u6-l5.3.en.en: Lucia is my friend. I live with her.
u6-l5.3.en.t: Lusiya — mening dugonam. Men u bilan yashayman.

u6-l5.3.why.en: Lucia is ona (she), and after s, ona becomes **ňou**. Ním is for on; ju is the object form, as in Mám ju rada.
u6-l5.3.why.t: Lusiya — ona (u), s soʻzidan keyin esa ona **ňou** boʻladi. Ním — on uchun, ju esa toʻldiruvchi shakli, masalan Mám ju rada.

u6-l5.4.prompt.en: Are you coming with us, Tomáš?

en: After **s**, pronouns take their instrumental forms: my becomes **nami**, so s nami = with us.
Tomáš is one friend, so use **ty**: ísť takes the ty form **ideš**. Idete is for vy.
t: **S** soʻzidan keyin olmoshlar inštrumentál shaklida keladi: my → **nami**, s nami = biz bilan.
Tomash — bitta doʻst, shuning uchun **ty** (sen): ísť ty shaklida keladi, **ideš** (borasan). Idete vy uchun.

u6-l5.5.en.en: Do you want to go with me?

u6-l5.6.title.en: Where? pred, za, nad, pod, medzi
u6-l5.6.title.t: Qayerda? pred, za, nad, pod, medzi

en: These five words also take the instrumental when they say where something is.
They work with pronouns too: pred **nami**, za **tebou**.
Feminine words without -a take **-ou** too: posteľ → pod posteľ**ou**.
t: Bu besh soʻz oʻzbekcha «oldida, orqasida…» kabi joyni bildiradi, lekin otdan oldin turadi. Narsa qayerda ekanini aytganda ular ham inštrumentál talab qiladi.
Ular olmoshlar bilan ham ishlaydi: pred **nami**, za **tebou**.
-a bilan tugamaydigan ayol jinsidagi soʻzlar ham **-ou** oladi: posteľ → pod posteľ**ou**.

en: I'm waiting in front of the restaurant.
The cat is under the table.

u6-l5.8.en.en: Tomáš is waiting in front of the university.

u6-l5.8.why.en: **Pred** (in front of) takes the instrumental, so feminine univerzita changes -a to **-ou**. Univerzitu is the object form.
u6-l5.8.why.t: **Pred** (oldida) inštrumentál talab qiladi, shuning uchun ayol jinsidagi univerzita soʻzida -a oʻrniga **-ou** keladi. Univerzitu — toʻldiruvchi shakli.

u6-l5.9.en.en: The café is between the bank and the post office.

u6-l5.9.why.en: **Medzi** (between) takes the instrumental for both places: bank**ou** a pošt**ou**.
u6-l5.9.why.t: **Medzi** (orasida) ikkala joy uchun ham inštrumentál talab qiladi: bank**ou** a pošt**ou**.

u6-l5.10.prompt.en: The cat is under the bed.

en: **Pod** (under) takes the instrumental when it says where. Feminine words without -a take **-ou** too: posteľ → **posteľou**.
Under is **pod**; nad means above. Both take the instrumental when they say where something is.
t: **Pod** (ostida) joyni bildirganda inštrumentál talab qiladi. -a bilan tugamaydigan ayol jinsidagi soʻzlar ham **-ou** oladi: posteľ → **posteľou**.
«Ostida» — **pod**, nad esa «tepasida». Ikkalasi ham narsa qayerdaligini bildirganda inštrumentál talab qiladi.

u6-l5.11.en.en: The lamp is above the table.

u6-l5.11.why.en: **Nad** (above) takes the instrumental: stôl adds **-om**, and its ô turns into o: **stolom**.
u6-l5.11.why.t: **Nad** (tepasida) inštrumentál talab qiladi: stôl **-om** oladi, ô esa o ga aylanadi: **stolom**.

u6-l5.12.why.en: **Za** (behind) takes the instrumental when it says where, and ty becomes **tebou**, as in s tebou. Teba is the form after pre: pre teba.
u6-l5.12.why.t: **Za** (orqasida) joyni bildirganda inštrumentál talab qiladi, ty esa **tebou** boʻladi, xuddi s tebou kabi. Teba esa pre soʻzidan keyin keladi: pre teba.

u6-l5.13.en.en: Marek is waiting behind the restaurant.

en: Mr Kováč is standing in front of the dorm.

u6-l6.titleEn.en: Let me take you to dinner

en: Three new patterns: **pozvať** (to invite), **piť** (to drink) and **niesť** (to carry). Learn the ja and oni forms; the rest follow.
**Žiť** (to live) goes like piť: žij**em**, žij**eš**, žij**e**…
Pozvať points to the future: Pozvem ťa. = I'll invite you.
t: Uchta yangi tuslanish: **pozvať** (taklif qilmoq), **piť** (ichmoq) va **niesť** (olib bormoq, koʻtarmoq). ja va oni shakllarini yodlang, qolganlari shularga oʻxshaydi.
**Žiť** (yashamoq) piť kabi tuslanadi: žij**em**, žij**eš**, žij**e**…
Pozvať kelajakni bildiradi: Pozvem ťa. = Seni taklif qilaman (keyinroq).

en: What are you drinking? — I'm drinking tea.
The waiter is carrying a beer.
**Jesť** (to eat) is irregular. Careful: **je** means both “is” and “eats”.
**Stať sa** (to become) takes the instrumental: stať sa lekár**om**, stať sa učiteľk**ou**. Like pozvať, it points to the future: Stanem sa lekárom. = I'll become a doctor.
t: **Jesť** (yemoq) qoidaga boʻysunmaydi. Ehtiyot boʻling: **je** ham «…dir» (byť feʼli: Marek je kuchár), ham «yeydi» degani.
**Stať sa** (boʻlmoq, aylanmoq) inštrumentál talab qiladi: stať sa lekár**om**, stať sa učiteľk**ou**. pozvať kabi u ham kelajakni bildiradi: Stanem sa lekárom. = Shifokor boʻlaman.

en: Marek is a cook. Now he's eating soup.
Emma wants to become a doctor.
t: Marek — oshpaz. Hozir u shoʻrva yeyapti.

u6-l6.3.en.en: What are you drinking, Emma? — I'm drinking tea.

u6-l6.3.why.en: The question is to Emma (ty), so the verb ends in **-š**: pij**eš**. Pije goes with on or ona, pijú with oni.
u6-l6.3.why.t: Savol Emmaga berilyapti (ty), shuning uchun feʼl **-š** bilan tugaydi: pij**eš** (ichyapsan). Pije on yoki ona bilan, pijú esa oni bilan keladi.

u6-l6.4.en.en: Lucia and Emma drink coffee with milk.
u6-l6.4.en.t: Lusiya va Emma sutli qahva ichadi.

u6-l6.4.why.en: Lucia and Emma are two people (they), so piť takes the oni form, **pijú**. Pije is for one person, pijeme for my (we).
u6-l6.4.why.t: Lusiya va Emma — ikki kishi (ular), shuning uchun piť oni shaklida keladi: **pijú**. Pije bitta kishi, pijeme esa my (biz) uchun.

u6-l6.5.en.en: Marek is carrying the soup to the table.

u6-l6.5.why.en: Marek is on (he), so niesť takes **nesie**. Nesú goes with oni, nesiem with ja.
u6-l6.5.why.t: Marek — on (u), shuning uchun niesť **nesie** boʻladi. Nesú oni bilan, nesiem esa ja bilan keladi.

en: The speaker is **ja**, so pozvať ends in **-em**: **pozvem** (I'll invite). Pozve goes with on or ona.
Lucia is the object of pozvem, so her name follows the feminine rule: -a changes to **-u**, **Luciu**.
**Pozvať na** takes the accusative, like pozývať na, so feminine večera changes -a to **-u**: na **večeru**.
t: Gapiruvchi — **ja**, shuning uchun pozvať **-em** bilan tugaydi: **pozvem** (taklif qilaman). Pozve on yoki ona bilan keladi.
Lusiya — pozvem feʼlining toʻldiruvchisi (oʻzbekchada «Lusiyani»), shuning uchun ism ayol jinsi qoidasiga boʻysunadi: -a oʻrniga **-u**, **Luciu**.
**Pozvať na** ham pozývať na kabi akuzatív talab qiladi, shuning uchun večera soʻzida -a oʻrniga **-u** keladi: na **večeru** (kechki ovqatga).

u6-l6.7.note.en: If they ask “Prídeš?” (Will you come?): Určite. (Definitely.) or Možno. (Maybe.)
u6-l6.7.note.t: Agar «Prídeš?» (Kelasanmi?) deb soʻrashsa: Určite. (Albatta.) yoki Možno. (Balki.)

u6-l6.8.question.en: Tomáš says “Pozvem ťa na večeru.” What's a natural reply?
u6-l6.8.question.t: Tomash «Pozvem ťa na večeru.» deydi. Qaysi javob mos keladi?

u6-l6.10.en.en: I'm eating fish and Lucia is eating chicken.
u6-l6.10.en.t: Men baliq yeyapman, Lusiya esa tovuq goʻshti yeyapti.

u6-l6.10.why.en: **Jesť** is irregular: with ja it's **jem**. Je goes with on or ona (Lucia je kuracie mäso), and also means “is”.
u6-l6.10.why.t: **Jesť** qoidaga boʻysunmaydi: ja bilan **jem**. Je on yoki ona bilan keladi (Lucia je kuracie mäso) va «…dir» maʼnosini ham beradi.

u6-l6.11.en.en: Emma and Lucia are eating fish with rice.
u6-l6.11.en.t: Emma va Lusiya guruch bilan baliq yeyapti.

u6-l6.11.why.en: Emma and Lucia are two people (they), so jesť takes its irregular oni form, **jedia**. Jeme is for my (we), je for one person.
u6-l6.11.why.t: Emma va Lusiya — ikki kishi (ular), shuning uchun jesť oʻziga xos oni shaklida keladi: **jedia**. Jeme — my (biz), je — bitta kishi uchun.

u6-l6.12.en.en: Lucia wants to become a teacher.

u6-l6.12.why.en: **Stať sa** (to become) takes the instrumental, so feminine učiteľka changes -a to **-ou**. Učiteľku is the object form.
u6-l6.12.why.t: **Stať sa** (boʻlmoq) inštrumentál talab qiladi, shuning uchun ayol jinsidagi učiteľka soʻzida -a oʻrniga **-ou** keladi. Učiteľku — toʻldiruvchi shakli.

en: “We” is **my**, and žiť goes like piť, so the my form is **žijeme**. Žijú is the oni form.
After **v** (in), the city changes its ending: v **Bratislave**, as in Žijem v Bratislave. This “where” case comes later; Bratislava is the plain form.
t: «Biz» — **my**, žiť esa piť kabi tuslanadi, shuning uchun my shakli — **žijeme** (yashaymiz). Žijú — oni shakli.
**V** soʻzidan keyin («Bratislavada») shahar nomining oxiri oʻzgaradi: v **Bratislave**, xuddi Žijem v Bratislave kabi. Bu kelishik keyinroq oʻrganiladi, Bratislava esa asosiy shakl.

en: Tomáš and Marek are drinking beer.

u6-l6.15.en.en: I want to become a cook.

u6-l6.15.why.en: After **chcieť**, the next verb is an infinitive, the -ť form: chcem sa **stať**. Stanem already means “I'll become”.
u6-l6.15.why.t: **chcieť** (xohlamoq) feʼlidan keyin keyingi feʼl infinitívda, yaʼni -ť shaklida keladi: chcem sa **stať**. Stanem esa «boʻlaman» degani.

u6-l7.1.prompt.en: I'll have the soup and fish with rice.
u6-l7.1.prompt.t: Men shoʻrva va guruch bilan baliq olaman.

en: After **s** (with), feminine nouns change -a to **-ou**: ryža → **ryžou**.
The fish is what you'll have, the object of dám si, so feminine ryba changes -a to **-u**: **rybu**.
**So** is only for words starting with s, z, š or ž. Ryžou starts with r, so plain **s** is right: s ryžou.
t: **S** (bilan) soʻzidan keyin ayol jinsidagi otlarda -a oʻrniga **-ou** keladi: ryža → **ryžou** (guruch bilan).
Baliq — siz oladigan narsa, dám si iborasining toʻldiruvchisi, shuning uchun ryba soʻzida -a oʻrniga **-u** keladi: **rybu**.
**So** faqat s, z, š yoki ž bilan boshlanadigan soʻzlar oldidan keladi. Ryžou r bilan boshlanadi, shuning uchun oddiy **s** toʻgʻri: s ryžou.

u6-l7.2.en.en: And to drink? — Mineral water, please.
u6-l7.2.en.t: Ichishga nima olasiz? — Mineral suv, iltimos.

u6-l7.2.why.en: The answer is a drink, so the question asks about drinking: **pitie** comes from piť (to drink). Jedlo is food, účet the bill.
u6-l7.2.why.t: Javob — ichimlik, demak savol ichish haqida: **pitie** soʻzi piť (ichmoq) feʼlidan. Jedlo — ovqat, účet — hisob.

u6-l7.5.why.en: **Za** (behind) takes the instrumental when it says where, so Tomáš adds **-om**. Tomáša is the object form.
u6-l7.5.why.t: **Za** (orqasida) joyni bildirganda inštrumentál talab qiladi, shuning uchun Tomáš **-om** oladi. Tomáša — toʻldiruvchi shakli.

en: Are you coming home with me?

u6-l7.7.en.en: Tomáš is going home by taxi.

u6-l7.7.why.en: For how you travel, the vehicle takes the instrumental without s: taxík**om**. S taxíkom would mean “with a taxi”.
u6-l7.7.why.t: Nimada borishni aytganda transport nomi **s qoʻshmasdan** inštrumentálda keladi: taxík**om** (taksida). S taxíkom «taksi bilan birga» degani boʻlardi.

u6-l7.8.question.en: How do you ask for the bill?

en: How you travel takes the instrumental, with no s: feminine električka changes -a to **-ou**, **električkou**.
t: Transport nomi s qoʻshmasdan inštrumentálda keladi: ayol jinsidagi električka soʻzida -a oʻrniga **-ou**, **električkou** (tramvayda).

u6-l7.10.en.en: Lucia, I'll take you out to dinner.
u6-l7.10.en.t: Lusiya, seni kechki ovqatga taklif qilaman.

u6-l7.10.why.en: With **ja**, pozvať ends in **-em**: pozv**em** (I'll invite). Pozve goes with on or ona, pozveme with my (we).
u6-l7.10.why.t: **ja** bilan pozvať **-em** bilan tugaydi: pozv**em** (taklif qilaman). Pozve on yoki ona bilan, pozveme esa my (biz) bilan keladi.

u6-l7.11.en.en: Tomáš is drinking beer with Marek.

u6-l7.12.prompt.en: Lucia wants to become a teacher.

en: **Stať sa** (to become) takes the instrumental, so feminine učiteľka changes -a to **-ou**: **učiteľkou**.
After **chce**, the next verb is an infinitive, the -ť form: **stať** sa. Stane already means “she'll become”.
t: **Stať sa** (boʻlmoq) inštrumentál talab qiladi, shuning uchun ayol jinsidagi učiteľka soʻzida -a oʻrniga **-ou** keladi: **učiteľkou**.
Chce (xohlaydi) feʼlidan keyin keyingi feʼl infinitívda, yaʼni -ť shaklida keladi: **stať** sa. Stane esa «u boʻladi» degani.

u6-l7.13.question.en: How do you say “The cat is under the table”?

u6-l7.13.why.en: **Pod** means under (nad is above). Saying where something is, it takes the instrumental: stôl → **stolom**.
u6-l7.13.why.t: **Pod** — «ostida» (nad — «tepasida»). Joyni bildirganda u inštrumentál talab qiladi: stôl → **stolom**.

u6-l7.14.en.en: How are you getting home, Mrs Horváthová?

u6-l7.14.why.en: Pani Horváthová is a teacher, so use polite **vy**: id**ete**. Ideš is for a friend (ty), idú for oni.
u6-l7.14.why.t: Horvatova xonim — oʻqituvchi, shuning uchun hurmatli **vy** (siz): id**ete**. Ideš — doʻstga (ty), idú esa oni uchun.
